chapter: Armstrong, Parker and life inside the Basie band
title: Meeting Louis Armstrong on a Coca-Cola box in Tulsa
summary: At the small hotel Tate sits with Armstrong in the alley and is told he will make it in New York.

bands.name: T. Holder's Twelve Clouds of Joy

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: All right, before we get back into the chronology, there's a couple things I want to pick up from yesterday, some loose ends.
First of all, you were going to tell me about meeting Louie.

Oh, yeah. Well, you remember I mentioned the small hotel where I first -- I mean, where I first heard Lester playing the tenor, the switch, you know, this is a small hotel where everybody used to go down in the lobby and jam, had a baby grand piano down there. So I was playing with this same T. Holder band and Louie played a one-nighter there -- had a big band during -- I think it was about 1931. Might have been '31. Anyway, -- and he was sitting out there -- we stayed there -- and he was sitting out in the alleyway on a Coca-Cola box with his socks all rolled down. This was about 1:00 in the day, they got in early. So I went up, I wanted to meet him, you know. I went up, I told him who I was, introduced myself. I says, 'I'm Buddy Tate, Mr. Armstrong, I'd like to meet you.' He says, 'Yeah, Pops.' He shook my hand. He says, 'Get you a box and sit down.' I said, 'Well --' I told him I was playing with Holder and I lived there in the hotel also. He said, 'Get you a box.' So I got a box, you know, and I sat down there and talked with

him and I told him that -- I says, "I sure would like to come to New York some day." "You'll make it." He says, "You'll make it." He says, -- I say, "Yeah, but everybody in New York -- I'm afraid of New York." He said, "Man, there's a lot of cats in New York can't play, you know."
